tools.name: cl

tools.name: tclsh
EVERYWHERE
tools.why: the sqlite corpus's testfixture TCL suite; tclsh also decides which Tcl header the corpus build compiles against. The unversioned formula deliberately, not tcl-tk@8: the corpus reads tclConfig.sh and supports Tcl 9, and the versioned formulae are keg-only, so their tclsh lands under /opt/homebrew/opt/<formula>/bin where neither the PATH nor the resolver's searched directories reach it. Finding a tclsh is not the same as knowing which Tcl a leg builds against - on macOS the name resolves to the system 8.5.9 while the corpus links Homebrew's 9.x - so the location belongs to the runner, not to this entry

EVERYWHERE

tools.name: qemu-x86_64

clock-step-probe.description: Counts the intervals in which this host's CLOCK_REALTIME diverged from CLOCK_MONOTONIC by more than the clock-step tolerance, and prints that count as 'steps='. The one runner here that is not work: it exists only to be checked, so that an expected exception which blames a clock step has something that can refuse to confirm it. The failing unit's own window stays the caller's - this runner measures the host it is asked on, when it is asked.

read-leg-path.description: Reads one path inside the leg's tree on the leg's own host - a file's trailing lines, optionally filtered by a regular expression, or a directory's newest entries - and prints and keeps it redacted, refusing any path outside the tree and any connection data or secret by name.

probe-reference-cc.description: Compiles one probe, or a batch of probes in ONE run (sources given as base64), with the reference compiler of the leg's own host, and prints and keeps the report redacted: the compiler's identity, the compile's exit code and diagnostics, and by mode the program's output and exit code, the assembly, a dump of the object, or what the compiler printed. A refused compile is reported as a measurement.

manual-end-to-end.description: Runs the MANUAL end-to-end corpus - entries whose cost makes them wrong to put in a gate, taken deliberately instead. Today that is the AArch64 branch-island edge, which fires only beyond the Imm26 field's reach, so witnessing it means compiling a single function larger than 134 MB. Its corpus is grouped by language at `.harness-config/runner/actions/manual-end-to-end/corpus/<language>/<name>/` and is invisible to both shipped corpus harnesses, which glob the `examples/` ROOT - so no entry here can move the default ctest count. Each entry must declare `manualRun: true` or this driver skips it by name.

macho-alias-ld64-matrix.description: Measures what Apple's ld64 does with a SECOND defined symbol at the same address as a canonical one, with and without -dead_strip. Eight cells: three producer variants (plain, altentry, setalias) crossed with dead-strip off/on while referencing ONLY the alias, plus a canonical-only control at both settings, and an n_desc dump per variant. Its answer is load-bearing and cited as evidence in src/link/format/macho.cpp and tests/link/test_macho_writer.cpp: a plain alias (n_desc = 0) is correct and N_ALT_ENTRY is not needed.

anchors.description: Read and lint deferred-anchor registry rows, and launch the one door that writes them, dssharness write-anchor and set-anchor.

apply-registry-row.description: Replace one deferred-anchor registry row with a lane's verbatim row text from a file.

burndown-queue.description: Re-derive the prioritized burndown queue from the registry, production errors first.

check-anchor-balance.description: Refuse a cycle that ends with more OPEN deferral-registry rows than it began.

check-anchor-registry.description: Refuse a `D-*` anchor cited in a scanned root that resolves to no registry row, and refuse a markdown table row whose unescaped pipes would silently drop cells.

check-diagnostic-codes.description: Refuse a duplicate, implicitly-numbered, or newly-uncovered `DiagnosticCode` ordinal.

check-doc-census.description: Refuse a documented figure that a census refutes, in prose or in a source comment, and repair it in place.

check-enum-name-table-guards.description: Refuse an `EnumNameTable` vocabulary declared in `src/` without a `DSS_CHECK_ENUM_NAME_TABLE` well-formedness assert.

check-export-macro-placement.description: Refuse DSS_EXPORT on a member of an already-exported class, which is MSVC error C2487.

check-guard-output-encoding.description: Refuse a Python script whose report cannot carry a non-cp1252 character through a pipe.

check-line-endings.description: Refuse a tracked text blob that carries a CR, and a CR instrument that cannot see one.

check-lsp-coordinates.description: Refuse a raw coordinate conversion in src/lsp/ outside lsp_coordinates.cpp — the anti-regression device for LSP positions resolved in synthesized preprocessor coordinates.

check-ninja-deps.description: Refuse a gate over a build directory whose objects recorded no header dependencies.

check-no-abort-in-tests.description: Refuse a new live `abort()` call site in test or test-support code.

check-orphan-tests.description: Refuse a test source that no CMake target compiles and no ctest entry runs.

check-path-identity.description: Refuse a second path canonicalizer -- path resolution lives in exactly one place.

check-pkg-pipeline.description: Pin the package pipeline's release-path step sequence and refuse an artifacts-only run that can reach a release.

check-plan-citations.description: Refuse a new `path:line` citation in the plans -- a citation names a stable reference, never a line number.

check-retyped-closed-sets.description: Census the diagnostics that RETYPE a closed vocabulary instead of projecting it.

check-scripts-index.description: Refuse an action that no index documents, an index entry that no action backs, and an action no runner can start.

check-stale-blockers.description: List OPEN registry rows whose Closing-work cell waits on a blocker that has since CLOSED.

check-stale-refusal-citations.description: Refuse a new present-tense refusal sentence that cites an anchor row already marked CLOSED.

check-wall-clock-in-tests.description: Refuse a new wall-clock duration literal in test code outside the shared measured budget.

check-wrapped-anchor-ids.description: Refuse a NEW anchor id split across a line break, which no grep can ever return.

cmake-import.description: Convert a CMake project into a DSS `.dss-project.json` manifest.

compile-bench.description: Time dsscp against gcc/clang/MSVC/tcc on ONE host over a subject size ladder, naming every reference it could not find.

corpus-census.description: Census the real-example corpus into a run-identified report instead of one overwritten log.

examples-census.description: Re-derive every corpus-manifest figure examples/README.md states, by parsing the manifests.

lane-fold.description: Seed a lane worktree from the main tree, fold only that lane's real changes back, and land it with its rows applied and its evidence preserved.

lane-worktree.description: Create and remove lane worktrees inside the ignored .worktrees/, refusing any root that would exceed Windows MAX_PATH.

owning-tree.description: Name the DSS tree a script's own file lives in -- walked up from that file, never taken from the caller's working directory or git environment.

pragma-profile-census.description: Census `#pragma` usage across the corpus and hold the profile to its expected shape.

profile-compile.description: Compile one fixed subject with a RELEASE dsscp on this host and report where the time went, so the HOST is the only variable across legs.

refresh_landing_log.description: Regenerate the PR landing-log hash anchors in the plans from git log.

sqlite.description: Prove dsscp builds SQLite from its real sources into the Tcl testfixture and the sqlite3 CLI, and runs SQLite's own unit corpus green, for every declared target.

sqlite-round-trip.description: Carry a sqlite leg's DSS-built artefacts to a machine that runs their target and prove they EXECUTE there (the round trip).

sqlite-runtime-bench.description: Measure the RUNTIME of an emitted sqlite3 binary, the standing runtime-differential instrument.

neverTransfer: candidate is name at any depth

sharedState.dsscp: the per-user runtime object cache (%LOCALAPPDATA%/dsscp/runtime-cache on Windows, $XDG_CACHE_HOME or ~/.cache/dsscp/runtime-cache elsewhere, DSS_RUNTIME_CACHE_DIR overriding both), one subdirectory per build stamp (version + commit + a digest of uncommitted changes), so a dsscp from another tree shares the directory but no entry; and the system temp directory
